title: The Perfect Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Merrick, founder of the coastal town of Greywater, is found empty during a centennial exhumation, retired detective Zephyrine Voss is pulled back into investigation by a town that once shunned him. The empty grave connects to three 'accidental' deaths Zephyrine quietly solved years ago, all tied to Merrick's contested will and a second, secret inheritance document hidden in his bookshop's foundations. As the tide threatens to wash away the evidence buried in the sea caves, Zephyrine realizes the killer is someone who has studied his own methods—and that the person he has come to love may be entangled in the plot. In the end, Zephyrine stages a false reveal of the inheritance document to force the killer's hand, chooses love over his lifelong duty to anonymity, and finally claims his place in Greywater as both its protector and its most visible citizen.
about_author: Lior Pemberton is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent a decade listening to local gossip behind a counter before turning it into fiction. They write mysteries about outsiders who solve what their communities would rather bury.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Zephyrine Voss, watching from his failing bookshop as the town exhuming founder Aldous Merrick's coffin discovers it empty. The crowd's murmurs turn toward old secrets, and Constable Ilsa Brandt—whom Zephyrine once helped unofficially—asks him to consult. Emotional beat: reluctant awakening; invisibility cracking.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, flashback-framed: he revisits the three deaths he solved privately—a fall from the lighthouse stairs, a boating mishap, a house fire—all beneficiaries or witnesses connected to Merrick's will. He never reported his findings, fearing exposure of his past. Emotional beat: guilt over silence compounding into resolve.

chapters.title: The Tide Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV as she shares the official case file, which contains details only the killer could know—an error in the drowning time that was never made public. Someone inside the investigation fed information out, or someone wrote the file itself. Emotional beat: professional unease; the case feels authored.

chapters.title: Marguerite at the Counter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: Marguerite Hale, the archivist helping organize Merrick's papers, spends an evening in the bookshop, and their slow-burning affection deepens. She mentions a missing codicil referenced but never filed in Merrick's estate. Emotional beat: warmth and belonging he doesn't trust himself to accept.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV: divers searching the sea caves near Merrick's cliffside estate find a rotted strongbox, empty except for a wax seal impression matching the missing codicil. The tide schedule suggests something else will surface within weeks. Emotional beat: dread—the killer is racing the water too.

chapters.title: The Founder's Circle
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: he interviews the surviving members of the Merrick family trust—Aldous's bitter nephew Corwin, charity director Odette Ferris, and lawyer Bram Quill—who each rehearse grief like lines from a play. One of them quotes a phrase from Zephyrine's own unpublished notes. Emotional beat: cold recognition that he is being watched.

chapters.title: Notes in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV: cataloguing Merrick's correspondence, she finds letters hinting he planned to disinherit everyone days before his death, then changed his mind after meeting someone unnamed. She hides the letter from Ilsa, unsure why. Emotional beat: first crack in her loyalty; love and suspicion braided together.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: Corwin Merrick survives a brake failure on the cliff road—identical in method to the lighthouse death Zephyrine solved years ago. The signature is unmistakable: the killer is repeating an old pattern deliberately, as if performing for him. Emotional beat: fury and fear; this is personal now.

chapters.title: Interrogating Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV: she reopens the three old cases officially, and the town turns hostile—Greywater prefers its accidents. Her superiors pressure her to close the file. She privately compares notes with Zephyrine and realizes he withheld evidence years ago. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Bookshop's Bones
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: repairing storm damage to his cellar, he finds a cavity in the foundation wall containing a sealed tin box—Merrick's hidden second will, naming an heir no one expects. Before he can read it fully, someone ransacks the shop above. Emotional beat: discovery shadowed by violation.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV: the will names Marguerite's late mother—Merrick's unacknowledged daughter—making Marguerite the sole heir. She swears she never knew, and Zephyrine believes her, but the evidence makes her the obvious suspect. Emotional beat: devastation; the woman he loves is now the prime target and suspect.

chapters.title: A Question of Alibis
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV: under pressure, Ilsa must formally investigate Marguerite, whose alibi for the night of the exhumation is thin. Zephyrine refuses to share what he knows, straining their partnership. Emotional beat: duty versus loyalty, mirrored across both investigators.

chapters.title: The Copyist
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: tracing the leaked case-file details, he identifies Bram Quill's clerk as the conduit—but the clerk is found drowned before he can talk, staged exactly like the boating accident. The killer is erasing the chain. Emotional beat: horror at the killer's patience and precision.

chapters.title: Odette's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV: Odette Ferris admits Merrick paid her for decades of silence about his illegitimate daughter, but denies killing anyone—she was being blackmailed by someone who knew about the codicil. A threatening note in her possession uses phrasing from Zephyrine's private notebooks. Emotional beat: vertigo; the killer has been inside Zephyrine's life for years.

chapters.title: Who Read My Notebooks
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: auditing who had access to his notes across two decades, he narrows to a handful—including, painfully, Marguerite, who catalogued his shop's archive last spring. He confronts her; she produces proof she never opened the boxes. Emotional beat: love tested by the habit of suspicion.

chapters.title: The Tide Table
chapters.summary: Isla's POV: reconstructing the killer's timeline against the tide tables, Ilsa realizes the final piece of evidence—the original codicil copy—was weighted and dropped in the caves, and the lowest tide of the year will expose it in four days. So will whatever else was sunk with it. Emotional beat: countdown urgency.

chapters.title: Corwin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: Corwin, terrified after the brake sabotage, offers to confess everything about the family's crimes if Zephyrine protects him. Through him, Zephyrine learns the killer's motive: not money, but erasure—destroying every trace of Merrick's true line so the founder's legend stays pure. Emotional beat: understanding the enemy's twisted devotion.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV: at the record low tide, the recovery team reaches the cave floor and finds the codicil's lead container—empty, replaced with a taunting note addressed to Zephyrine by name, quoting his first-ever case. The killer wanted them here, watching the wrong thing. Emotional beat: trap sprung; humiliation and clarity at once.

chapters.title: The Reveal That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV: realizing the killer cannot resist correcting the record, Zephyrine publicly announces he has authenticated a copy of the codicil and will read it at the bookshop—bait. He and Ilsa stage the reading while Marguerite, wearing a wire, watches the crowd. Emotional beat: controlled terror; the invisible man making himself the loudest thing in town.

chapters.title: The Devoted Hand
chapters.summary: Climax, shifting between Zephyrine's and Ilsa's POVs: the killer—Merrick's aged former secretary, guardian of the founder's myth since childhood—strikes during the reading, confessing mid-assault that she emptied the grave to prove Merrick ascended body and soul. Ilsa subdues her; Zephyrine takes a knife wound protecting Marguerite. Emotional beat: violence breaking the town's long silence.

chapters.title: Reading the Will
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV: weeks later, the genuine codicil is read aloud; Marguerite inherits modestly and donates the estate to the town, dissolving the founder's myth into something honest. The community that once looked through Zephyrine now looks to him. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, closing chapter: recovering in the bookshop above the repaired cellar, Zephyrine hangs a new sign and, for the first time, keeps his door unlocked. He and Marguerite sort the archive together, and Ilsa brings him a fresh file—one accident too many in the next town over. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the detective chooses to be seen, and to continue.
